items.title: Jordan Rodgers Calls Brother Aaron's Steelers Departure 'Sad to See'
items.summary:
Jordan Rodgers is admittedly shocked by his brother Aaron Rodgers ’ departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers.

“That was something we weren’t all preparing for,” Jordan, 38, quipped on the Friday, November 27, broadcast of Good Morning America . “It was a crazy couple days for the Steelers and Aaron. I think that first and foremost, it’s just kind of sad to see it end this way in Pittsburgh.”

He continued, “There was so much good vibes and hope about the reuniting of [Mike] McCarthy and Rodgers and the potential to make a playoff run one last dance. Unfortunately, it didn’t happen that way.”

Aaron, 42, signed with the Steelers in 2025. The team benched him from Friday’s game, shortly before the quarterback claimed that head coach McCarthy, 63, was “unhealthy” in a bombshell interview. While McCarthy has refuted the claims , the Steelers have since parted ways with Aaron.

Jordan Rodgers Makes 1st Comments About Brother Aaron Since Reconciliation 

“I think what’s getting lost in this, though, is just how unacceptable and unprecedented some of the behavior that McCarthy has displayed and how unique that is,” Jordan added on Friday. “I think I would be surprised if he continued to be the head coach moving forward, whether that’s short-term, long-term, whatever it is. I think, having been in locker rooms … there’s too many jobs at stake for people to put up with that behavior.”

He speculated, “I think the Steelers will look into this, but seemingly, the accusations and allegations are confirmed in a lot of ways, and he didn’t refute them. Crazy world that we’re living in,…
items.t: Jordan Rodgers Calls Brother Aaron's Steelers Departure 'Sad to See'

items.title: Hayden Panettiere's Ex Brian Hickerson 'Distraught' After Her Death
items.summary:
The brother of Hayden Panettiere ’s on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson , is sharing an update on how he is doing following her tragic death in August .

“I spent almost eight to 10 weeks up in Greenville [South Carolina] around him,” Zach Hickerson said in an interview with TMZ published on Friday, November 27. “One word that comes to mind is just distraught, heartbroken, confused. I know that there’s still a certain level of shock and surrealness to him of that. There’s just no resolve to this. This isn’t, like, a legal thing. This isn’t a breakup thing. … It’s a definitive thing, and there’s no fixing [it]. There’s no resolve.”

“He’s, one, navigating the loss [and] two … trying to look ahead at the next chapter of his life or the rest of his life. Like, what now?” Zach, 39, continued. “Given all that’s happened, given the reputation, I just know that he’s carrying a lot. Rightfully so, to an extent.”

Panettiere was pronounced dead at the scene after authorities responded to a 911 call at an Airbnb in Greenville, South Carolina, on August 16. The Heroes actress was staying at the residence with Brian, 37. Zach was also present.

Brother of Hayden Panettiere's Ex Recalls Her Last Moments Before Death 

“I know that he’s heartbroken,” Zach shared on Friday. “I’ve tried to be there as much as I can for him. About three or four weeks ago, I realized that, man, I was probably trying to carry a little bit too much for everyone else and had not really dealt with the grief and loss myself. So I’ve taken the last two to three weeks to really kind of be on my own, so it’s hard for…

Princess Kate Middleton has been named patron of leading cancer hospital The Christie more than two years after going public with her own cancer battle .

Kensington Palace said in a statement on Friday, November 27, “The announcement follows Her Royal Highness’s visit to The Christie’s Withington site in June 2026, where she met patients, families and staff and learned more about the hospital’s internationally renowned approach to supporting people living with and beyond cancer.”

The Christie in Manchester, England, is one of the world’s leading cancer treatment centers and the largest of its kind in Europe.

“The patronage reflects the Princess of Wales’s longstanding interest in the role that emotional, social and physical well-being play in cancer patients’ journeys, and her commitment to highlighting the importance of holistic care alongside world-class clinical treatment,” Kensington Palace said. “Building on her recent work exploring recovery, resilience and life beyond diagnosis, the patronage reflects a shared belief in supporting the whole person throughout their cancer journey and beyond.”
